newsitem.title: JAPAN: Analyst lowers Nippon Steel's earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Analyst lowers Nippon Steel's earnings forecast.

text.p: Nippon Steel Corp's parent current profit for the business year ending on March 31 could be 10 billion yen lower than a previous forecast of 85 billion yen due to a fire at its Oita plant, said Toru Nagai, analyst at Morgan Stanley Japan Ltd.
The September 24 fire resulted in the plant's hot-rolling line being shut for two months, Nippon Steel said this week.
Nagai said additional labour and shipment costs to shift production to other plants would boost operational costs by 10 billion yen.
He also said the company would likely post an extraordinary loss of five billion yen to repair the damage.
As a result, Nagai said his forecast of the company's net profit for the 1996/97 business year would now be 30 billion yen, down from his previous forecast of 40 billion yen.
On a consolidated basis, current profit for the 1996/97 business year is now expected to be 73 billion yen, down from the previous forecast of 83 billion yen, he said.
Meanwhile, the company would likely see a consolidated net loss of three billion yen, down from a net profit of seven billion yen as previously forecast, he said.
